body:
It works fine on with Firefox here. The German keyboard may be the issues though.
Could you figure out what's the `event.keyCode` for A, S and D in your keyboard?

I used the console logging in webgl_camera.html, and confirmed that the keycodes are as expected (ASCII character are mainly unchanged in European keyboards). Same problem with that programm, cannot use o and p, always opens search.

I also tested with all Add-ons disabled. Firexfox 12.0, confirmed on two other computers (32 bit and 64 bit).

I also disabled autohokey to be sure, no change. No autohotkey on the other computers I had used.

Same problem with Firefox 13 beta
Have you tried on another computer or another german pal?
Yes (see above), tried on three computers. I just tried with Firefox 11, same problem.

And does it happend with this example?
http://mrdoob.github.com/three.js/examples/misc_camera_trackball.html

Yes. See http://www.menne-biomed.de/uni/camera.png for a screen shot (with webgl_camera, the problem is easier to isolate there because no problem with multiple keydowns.)

!!!! See your query below !!!!
The example in the screenshot is not the one I posted, neither it uses trackball camera... ?
Anyway, I can't really reproduce it myself. But let me know if you find out what may be causing the issue.

``` javascript
event.preventDefault();
```

in onKeyDown did it for camera. The same should be in the trackball. And probably another half dozen of key Event I found where it could be relevant.

Can you try with this build?
https://raw.github.com/mrdoob/three.js/dev/build/Three.js
Also for me it works ok (Win7). Maybe it's some Firefox extension causing this?

Checked details today: The modification works, but blocks all other keys. I think it should be change to preventDefault only when a requested key is pressed, but not for all keys.

Suggested change (tested here): add event.preventDefault to both (!!) if (_state !===STATE.NONE) in TrackballControls.

I found out why this problem cannot be reproduced on your site: On all our computers, in Firefox we have enabled:;
(Sorry, translated from German)

Settings
Extended
General
Start search on typing.

When you disable it, the original version of trackball (and all keyboard-examples) works as expected. However, this is a valid setting, so better defend against it with the preventDefault method.

> Checked details today: The modification works, but blocks all other keys. I think it should be change to preventDefault only when a requested key is pressed, but not for all keys.

Yep, I noticed that. Sounds like a good solution :)
